newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds play it safe again.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds play it safe again.

text.p: *Australia bonds were little changed from Thursday's closing levels as the market took a cautious stance ahead of the key U.S. jobs data, and more importantly, next week's RBA meeting.
*September retail data seen raising chances of a rate cut.
Australian bonds were little changed from Thursday's closing levels as the market took a cautious stance ahead of the key U.S. jobs data later on Friday.

The market also continues to find difficulty maintaining a rally as an expected 50 basis point easing in official interest rates is fully factored in, and until it is endorsed, yields are seen stuck at current 32-month lows, analysts said.
However, the market will not have to wait too much longer for a decision on policy with the Reserve Bank meeting on Tuesday, and further evidence today suggested they may ease.
September monthly and quarterly retail trade released today were both weaker than expected, down 3.7 percent and up 0.6 percent respectively.

"The retail trade figures were yet another indicator showing weakness in the economy," said Hans Kunnen, chief economist at Colonial State Bank. "We expect a 50 (basis) point easing in November, but beyond that we are not so sure the Reserve Bank will move again."
The bonds firmed on the data, but again failed to make much impression on recent yield lows, but bill futures held gains going into the close.

The December bill futures contract ended at 93.52, pointing to a cash rate of 6.48 percent by its December 12 maturity, while March 1997 bill were at 93.72, indicating a rate of 6.28 percent. Official interest rates currently stand at 7.0 percent.

The Reuters Australian monthly interest rate poll of economists released today showed the median probability of an interest cut by end-November at 65 percent and 80 percent by the end of the year. A similar poll was carried out last week which showed respective chances at 60 and 75 percent.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries were firm going into today's jobs report after Thursday's friendly U.S. data.
Forecasts centre on a 212,000 rise for October non-farm payrolls after the surprise 40,000 fall in September.
The market's cautious stance saw spreads to other dollar bloc bonds widen again and the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread now stands some 20 basis points higher than last Friday.
